subject: For the violation of multivariate normality assumption: lavaan or piecewiseSEM?

messages.author: b48ebf16ed4cffef
messages.subject: For the violation of multivariate normality assumption: lavaan or piecewiseSEM?
parts:
Hello again, 

I was wondering, all else being equal, which is the better choice for endogenous variables measured as count data that violate the multivariate normality assumption of SEM: sem model in lavaan with bootstrap estimates for standard errors and adjusted chi-squared value or glm in piecewiseSEM with Poisson-distribution error? Specifically, I'm interested how environmental variables determine  species richness of predators and of their prey in different sites along an environmental gradient. Following the O’Hara and Kotze (2010) recomendations in Methods in Ecology and Evolution, I don't want log-transform these data, but I also don't know what to do. Is there any advantage to choosing one approach over another? I don't find any answer on internet. I only found that for models misspecified and nonnormal data Lai (2018) indicates the lavaan and bootstraps. With this method, however, he warns of the problem of sample size below 250 could generate inaccurate parameter estimates; my sample size is exactly 59.

Thank you,

O’Hara and Kotze (2010) 10.1111/j.2041-210X.2010.00021.x
Lai (2018) DOI: 10.1080/10705511.2017.1392248
